newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain consumer boom seen bypassing some retailers.
newsitem.headline: Spain consumer boom seen bypassing some retailers.

text.p: Despite a bright outlook for Spanish consumption for the rest of the year, the glow will not rub off on all retailers equally, analysts warned on Thursday.

Wednesday's release of first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), which showed the consumer side of the economy booming, provided a fresh dynamo for retail stocks. But many analysts say they are now around or, in some cases, beyond fair value.
And although analysts see consumption growth either maintained or even accelerating in remaining quarters this year, this still did not justify the huge rise in retailers' shares.
"Consumption is growing very strongly, but we have to differentiate clearly between companies," said Julio Mas, analyst at Merrill Lynch in Madrid.
"That growth does not seem to be reaching food items for the moment, and the reaction (of food retailers) in the stock market in the past two days has been a bit excessive," he said.

Hypermarkets Pryca and Continente shares gained 6.98 and 8.49 percent respectively on Wednesday. At 1355 GMT, Pryca was up a further 3.1 percent to 3,160 pesetas and Continente was up 2.61 percent to 3,345 pesetas.
At the same hour Cortefiel was up 11.04 percent to 6,740 pesetas, against an Ibex blue-chip index rise of around 0.01 percent to 6,913.86.
Sales growth at hypermarkets has not mirrored private consumption, which rose 2.8 percent in the first quarter year- on-year and 1.0 percent versus the previous quarter.
Pryca said its gross sales data for the five months to May fell 0.5 percent year-on-year, although sales picked up in May versus April this year.
Furthermore experts said it is difficult to tell, because of the lack of retail indicators in Spain, exactly which type of shops are benefiting from more demand.
Complicating matters further, first-quarter GDP figures were boosted by seasonal factors.

"Holy week fell in March this year, so while first quarter consumption figures look better versus last year, we're going to see the opposite effect in the second quarter," said Javier Requena, analyst at Benito y Monjardin (B&M) brokerage.
To add further fuel, the bull run in the stock market at the moment means that any news is good news, analysts said.
"Really we're seeing once again how things are being blown up out of proportion (regarding the stock market)," he added.
Poor liquidity also means that any movements in these stocks tends to be sharp, analysts said.
B&M are recommending selling Pryca and Continente.

"Hypermarkets are trading at (price-earnings) ratios of around 25, which seems excessive if you think that they're looking at profits growth of about 10 percent this year and next," B&M's Requena said.
Clothing outlets Cortefiel and Adolfo Dominguez, and fast food chain Telepizza were better bets in this scenario, while hotel group Sol Melia is also expected to gain from the consumer drive.

"Cortefiel will have noticed (the rise in consumption) I estimate that its sales have grown around 15 percent (in the first quarter), although part of that reflects calendar differences (between Holy Week in 1996 and 1997)," Merrill's Mas said.
Another analyst said Cortefiel, Pryca and Continente are now trading above his year-end target price.
Cortefiel was targeted at 6,100 pesetas, Pryca at 3,150 pesetas and Continente at 2,900-3,000 pesetas.
But BBV Interactivos sees Pryca bound for 3,400 pesetas, although Continente is now also trading above their 3,300 peseta target.
Longer term, more detailed information may be necessary to make accurate estimates regarding the sector.

"The problem (with the GDP figures) is that really no-one knows exactly where this 2.8 percent rise in consumption has been concentrated...it's clear that there are changes in (spending) habits going on, but we don't have access to any specialised data which tells us where that is," Requena said.
